nodes.text: A year of steady growth, and the plan that carries it into the next decade.
Results, retention and the numbers behind them
Three findings that change the plan
Budget, hiring and the risks we carry
The year in numbers, and what sits behind each of them.
Growth that we can explain is the only kind we want to keep.
Dana Whitfield, in the FY2026 letter to partners
Net revenue retention held above 118% in every quarter, before any new logo.
Deals between 200 and 2,000 seats closed twice as fast as a year ago.
Partners now bring a third of pipeline
Referred deals close at higher values and churn less.
Every team ran its own playbook
Handoffs lost a day at every step
A single flow every team adopts
Handoffs measured and cut to hours
Double the segment team and ship the two integrations every deal asks for.
Certifications, regional residency and a support tier that answers in an hour.
A free tier that grows into paid on its own, measured weekly.
Sessions start when they say; nobody waits well.
Each session ends with a round.
Notes on paper; photos of the board at the end.
Demos are brave. Questions are curious.
Up from $36.8M, with expansion ahead of new business for the first time.
Held above target in every quarter; enterprise accounts led.
Mid-market grew fastest; churn fell to 4.1% on the year.
Before the round, at the current burn and the current plan.
Expansion overtook new business in Q2 and has led every quarter since.
Expansion revenue in Q4, a record
Share of Q4 growth from existing customers
Segment team hired, the two integrations shipped, pricing page rebuilt.
Certifications complete, EU residency live, one-hour support tier launched.
Free tier public, conversion measured weekly, first paid upgrades on their own.
Double down on the channel that grew, cut the ones that did not.
A 45-minute call maps your workflow and the numbers you care about.
One team, two weeks, your real data. We measure against the baseline.
Every team onboarded in waves, with a named lead on each side.
A quarterly session on the numbers, and the plan for the next one.
Badges, maps and the good espresso.
Off the grill, by the fire.

Night one ends
around the fire.
A book or a deck of cards
A timber lodge at altitude with a lake, a library, a long porch and no reason to check messages.

Selling online is
still built for
big brands.
Most small shops still cannot take an order online.
Store builders demand weeks of setup and fees.
Marketplaces skim a third and keep the customer.
We read a shop's socials and point of sale, then assemble a ready-to-sell storefront with payments and delivery included.
Twenty years across three funds; leads the portfolio.
Built the operating model every team now runs on.
Owns the roadmap and the free tier that feeds it.
Retention, expansion and the partners who bring both.
They did not sell us software. They showed us the number we were losing every week, and then made it stop.
Questions now, or any time this week. The deck and the model are in the shared folder.
